hero.name: Fay Lyu (HazezZ)
hero.subtitle: Optimization · Formal Methods · Game Theory · Data
hero.positioning: I work at the intersection of optimization, formal methods, and data-oriented modeling. My current research-facing work includes Isabelle/HOL formalization of submodular greedy guarantees, optimization reading/research in ORIE, and prototype-building that turns structured intuition into reproducible pipelines. This page is a short research entry point (interests, current projects, and links). For internships, engineering deployment details, and broader application-facing summaries, see the CV page.

interests.title: Research interests (current)
items: Optimization theory (especially algorithmic structure and first-order methods)
Game theory (especially as a mathematical modeling language for strategic structure)
Formal methods for mathematics (Isabelle/HOL, proof structure, reusability)
I care about explicit assumptions, reusable abstractions, and verifiable reasoning

projects.title: An Ongoing Isabelle Research Project: Formalising Submodular Greedy
projects.problem: Formalize the classical greedy (1−1/e) approximation guarantee for monotone submodular maximization under a cardinality constraint.
projects.method: Split the development into constructive and approximation-analysis layers, then encode assumptions and intermediate lemmas explicitly in Isabelle/HOL.
projects.contribution: Building reusable formal scaffolding + documenting design choices and proof decomposition as a research log.

projects.title: Spring 2026 | A New Research Direction (Cornell ORIE)
projects.problem: Understand which dual / lower-bound framework gives nontrivial information for a graph-relative-difference distance-fitting objective (B-encoded), with current focus on constrained/composite first-order structure and duality.
projects.method: Compare DC/Fenchel-based dualization against plain Lagrangian duals, and analyze where relaxation becomes too loose (unconstrainedness / translation invariance / non-identifiability).
projects.current_status: Right now we’re trying to understand which dual framework gives nontrivial information for this distance-fitting objective. The DC/Fenchel route gives a clean conjugate-based dual with explicit domain conditions, while the most natural plain Lagrangian duals turn out to be too loose and collapse to the trivial bound 0 due to unconstrainedness and translation invariance. The next step is to tighten the relaxation (e.g., via gauge-fixing and/or an augmented Lagrangian / ADMM viewpoint) to obtain an informative bound or an algorithmically useful dual.
projects.contribution: Dual-framework comparison, structural diagnosis of degeneracy, and research-note documentation of the evolving problem formulation.

projects.title: Metalcore Piano Lab | From Audio to Chart (WIP)
projects.problem: Map continuous audio (or MIDI) into a playable rhythm-game style chart as a structured discretization problem.
projects.method: Onset/beat detection, tempo tracking, segmentation, alignment, and playability-oriented constraints.
projects.contribution: Browser-native prototype + research-style documentation of assumptions, failure modes, and next optimization targets.

now_section.title: What I’m Currently Thinking About
now_section.lead: Questions and themes I’m actively using to steer reading, proof work, and modeling choices.

now_items: Which dual formulations remain informative under non-identifiability / translation invariance, and which collapse to trivial lower bounds.
How to design reusable proof structure in Isabelle/HOL so formalization artifacts scale beyond one theorem statement.
When a “natural” relaxation is too loose: what structural fix (gauge-fixing, constraints, augmentation) restores useful information.
How signal-like inputs (audio, temporal traces) can be mapped into discrete, computable structures without losing interpretability.
How optimization / formal methods / modeling can share one language of explicit assumptions and reproducible abstractions.
